function: Learns AAV movement and excitation current (beamforming) weights of a collaborative-beamforming virtual antenna array, trading achievable rate to a mobile ground user against flight energy (pp. 7, 9).
system: 8 or 16 rotary-wing AAVs forming a virtual antenna array to one mobile ground user, one interfering BS; no RIS; 2.4 GHz; Rician fading (pp. 4, 5, 13).
method: Evolutionary multi-objective deep RL (EMOPPO-VLH): PPO with LSTM actor/critic, vectorized value function, hyper-sphere task selection; trained by interaction with a simulator, centralized (pp. 9-13).
data_channel: Custom simulated air-to-ground channel: path loss with exponent 2 and Rician small-scale fading, Gauss-Markov user mobility; mathematical-model simulator, no dataset or measurements (pp. 5, 6, 13).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and testing; two swarm sizes (8, 16 AAVs); robustness tests (phase error, damaged AAV, jitter) only in the online appendix (pp. 13, 16).
baselines: Non-learned: MOEA/D and MOPSO (multi-objective evolutionary algorithms). Learned: EDDPG, ETD3, EPPO, EPPO with GRU, all evolutionary multi-objective RL variants (p. 14).
metrics: Total achievable rate f1, total AAV flight energy f2, inverted generational distance (IGD), hypervolume (HV) (pp. 14-15).
complexity: Order O(Gmax n nevo (sum_l m_{l-1} m_l + M)) for the proposed method; MOEA/D and MOPSO O(G N^2); no runtime reported (pp. 13-14).
q1_support: p. 5: "modeled as a Rician distribution"; p. 13: "rather than relying on pre-collected real-world data". Not met: the channel is a custom simulator (path loss with Rician fading, p. 5); the text says the models are "derived from real-world data" (p. 13) but names no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or other standardized model and uses no measured dataset.
q2_support: p. 16: "the robustness of the proposed approach is assessed under various unexpected" scenarios, with details in Appendix C, which is online and not in the PDF; p. 13: "and retrain the DRL algorithm" is the stated answer to environment changes. Not met: no test of a trained policy in an unseen condition and no reported adaptation appear in the 18 pages.
q3_support: p. 14: "two multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs)" (MOEA/D and MOPSO, non-learned); p. 14: "two multi-policy MORLs, namely, evolutionary deep deterministic policy gradient (EDDPG)" (learned, with ETD3); p. 15: "outperforms all other optimization approaches across both scales" (rate f1, energy f2, IGD, HV).
q4_support: p. 13: "The total complexity of the proposed EMOPPO-VLH is given by O(Gmax" (order of complexity of the proposed method); p. 14: "leading to an overall complexity of" (orders of the baselines MOEA/D and MOPSO).
q5_support: p. 13: "rather than relying on pre-collected real-world data". Not met: the policy is trained in a simulator built from mathematical models; p. 1: "supplementary downloadable material available at" a DOI, which the text describes only as Appendices A to D, with no statement that code or data are released.
notes: Area 6 by the tie-break order (6 before 3): the aerial link is controlled through the excitation current (beam) weights, learned jointly with the AAV trajectories, which are above the physical layer, so the work passes the above_phy rule for aerial links (pp. 7, 9). ris=0: no RIS in the system. q2=0: the PDF reports no test in unseen conditions; the scalability and robustness results (AAV number, user mobility, phase errors, damaged AAV, jitter) are only in the online Appendix C (p. 16) and p. 13 says a changed environment or AAV number calls for retraining, so the reviewer may revisit q2 if that appendix is available. q3=1 needs confirmation: EPPO and EPPO with GRU are ablations and are not counted; EDDPG and ETD3 put standard DDPG and TD3 inside the authors' evolutionary framework (p. 14). q4=1 from the stated order of complexity (p. 13); the detailed analysis is in the online Appendix A.2. q5=0: the DOI on p. 1 leads to supplementary material that the text describes only as appendices.
